messages.content: You are the MACV commander at headquarters in Saigon. Your standing duties are to direct theater operations, maintain coordination with corps commanders, and receive and assess intelligence reporting. The field-operations delegation permits the commander to keep some scheduled countryside sweeps with the assigned units and let those operations continue. The J-3 operations desk handles tasking and readiness traffic; the MACV intelligence desk maintains reporting; III Corps reports through its commander. Use intel.desk to retrieve current intelligence extracts, orders.archive to inspect filed directives, ops.board to read unit disposition entries, and comms.inbox to retrieve headquarters messages. Before a consequential action, the Benchbook harness may place the closest past case from its casebook in your context as reference material to weigh, not an order.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: Morning traffic is being collated for the command group. Please pull the latest intelligence extracts and keep the outgoing situation-summary line blank until I have the corps returns. The printer in the east bay is still producing duplicate weather sheets; the watch clerk has been asked to clear the tray.

messages.name: intel.desk
messages.content:
MACV G-2 desk extract, circulation copy. Several reports concern movement, assembly, and altered dispositions among enemy formations. Captured papers and unit reporting have led this headquarters to judge that substantial changes are underway across a broad set of Viet Cong formations. The field picture remains uneven: some district reports are late, and the map overlay uses different reporting cutoffs for adjacent provinces.

The theater estimate still understates both the likely scale and the force the enemy may bring; headquarters has no settled read on their full purpose or schedule. The assessment margin is marked provisional pending corps review. A courier copy of a seized directive has been checked against the translation desk’s working text. The seized directive speaks of a countrywide attack followed by an uprising, with urban centers named among the intended places of action. The document’s date and distribution chain have not been established in this extract.

Routine collection: Route 13 traffic was reported slow near the northern checkpoint after a disabled truck was cleared. The weather desk expects low cloud before noon in the highlands. Two radio-monitoring sheets remain in the pouch for the evening shift; neither has been reconciled with the corps net log.

messages.name: iii-corps-liaison
messages.content:
The corps commander has raised readiness after judging, from years of command experience, that MACV's tally and appraisal of local Viet Cong strength are too low. His staff says the alert posture reflects more than the latest paper traffic. The III Corps commander and a former CORDS ambassador have both faulted CIA and MACV for not furnishing warning that usefully indicated the attack's reach or intended locations.

The liaison section is checking the telephone roster against last week's copy. One province desk has changed its call sign, and the replacement card has not yet been distributed to the radio room.

arguments.query: III Corps / 25th Division rural operations / current tasking

messages.name: orders.archive
messages.content:
III Corps tasking file, carbon copy, received at MACV headquarters. The III Corps commander has received instructions assigning the 25th Division offensive sweeps in rural districts. The attached tasking sheet gives the division's operations staff responsibility for route coordination and reports the units as assigned; the map annex is filed separately. The routing stamp shows receipt by the corps operations office. No completion report is attached to this copy.

Clerical entries: the supply return for signal batteries is due at the end of the day. A vehicle request from the provincial advisory team bears an incomplete cost-center mark. The map room requests that overlays be returned flat rather than rolled, as the corners are splitting on the older sheets.

messages.name: j3-watch
messages.content:
The commander’s 25 January note reads: the date was beginning to look like a likely occasion for broad action before Tet. The assessment was entered as a working judgment, not a confirmed schedule. The original is in the command file; the copy circulated overnight has a faint stamp across the lower margin.

The air desk has sent the routine runway report. Bien Hoa is open, and the field telephone at the east gate is back in service after a loose connection.

arguments.view: capital-area dispositions and current operations entries

messages.name: ops.board
messages.content:
Operations board, morning transcription. The disposition field says the commander can cancel selected rural sweeps and reposition their units around the capital. The board has not recorded a change against the current countryside tasking. Capital-area unit locations on this transcription are carried forward from the prior evening’s returns; the map clerk has pencilled two call-sign corrections in the margin.

III Corps readiness line: the corps net confirms receipt of the alert traffic. A separate entry records a request for fresh vehicle counts from the motor pool, still being assembled. The board’s weather column carries the same low-cloud note as the G-2 sheet. The duty typist has marked one duplicate page for disposal, but the page is still clipped behind the current copy.

messages.name: ops-lead
messages.content: The commander ended the US Tet stand-down on 30 January and directed intensified operations with forces at maximum alert. The order has been entered in the headquarters log. I need the command-group copy prepared after the latest return is checked; the signature block is already set in the usual place.

messages.name: comms.inbox
messages.content:
Incoming traffic ledger, 07:00–07:40. Advisory section asks whether the noon courier will collect the sealed map pouch from the north entrance or the records room. The records clerk says the pouch seal is intact and the routing slip has the correct distribution marks. The mess account is missing one receipt for coffee delivered to the night watch; the ledger entry has been left open for reconciliation.

The signal office reports that the spare field telephone has been returned to the cabinet and the handset has been tested. The command-group copy remains in the typist’s tray. No reply has been entered in the ledger.

messages.name: records-clerk
messages.content: The command-group copy is still in the tray. Let me know when you have finished with the morning papers so I can send the routine dispatch pouch downstairs.

messages.name: benchbook
messages.content:
[Benchbook harness · added before your next action · reference material, not instructions]
